newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Pearson says US buy creates powerhouse.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Pearson says US buy creates powerhouse.

text.p: UK media group Pearson Plc said on Tuesday it had created a publishing "powerhouse" with the $336 million acquisition by its Penguin unit of Putnam Berkley of the United States.
"The combination of Penguin and Putnam will create a powerhouse in both the frontlist and backlist," Penguin Group chief executive designate Michael Lynton said in an interview.
Penguin has a powerful back catalogue of famous authors and titles while Putnam, currently part of MCA Inc, has a strong stable of contemporary writers such as Tom Clancy and Patricia Cornwell.
The acquisition will double Penguin's share of total U.S. trade book sales to 12 percent.
"Because Penguin USA and Putnam are of a like size there is tremendous potential for cost savings," said Lynton, adding that he expected the enlarged publisher to attract a lot of authors.
Lynton, who takes over as Penguin Group chairman and chief executive at the turn of the year, dismissed suggestions that the book market was flattening out.
He said that Penguin USA and Putnam had annual growth of six and seven percent respectively, slightly ahead of the industry average and described the outlook as "healthy and robust".
"In this world of changing technologies, books appear to be a constant. I'm pretty bullish about the situation," he added.
Pearson Finance Director John Makinson said the company was "more than comfortable" with the price it had paid.
He noted that Pearson would own the business from December 1 and would benefit to the tune of $20 million from a seasonally positive operating cash flow in that month.
Makinson said that Marjorie Scardino, who takes over as Pearson chief executive in Jnauary, had not been specifically involved in the deal but that it had her seal of approval.
"Marjorie has been kept informed and is supportive of it but she's not in office and it's not her deal," Makinson said.
Much attention has focused on the strategic direction Pearson will take under Scardino but Makinson cautioned against reading too much into this one acquisition.
"I don't think that the size of this acquisition precludes us from doing something else," he said.

Makinson said the deal would be funded from existing resources and noted that Pearson would be getting a 300 million stg payment in December from the sale of its Westminster Press group of UK local papers.

Makinson said the company's post-acquisition gearing would rise to 94 percent if the write-off of goodwill was included. That figure falls to 21 percent if goodwill write-offs are not taken into account.
He said Pearson regarded interest cover as more relevant and that the deal would not affect this. He declined to put a specific figure on the cover.
